reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource report, supplied resource-review context, deterministic aggregate, direct NamingSystem behavior findings, shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, and selected R4/R6 NamingSystem StructureDefinition elements. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, per the review scope.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 NamingSystem was trial-use/FMM 1, so compatibility burden is weak compared with mature or normative resources. That softens the case for revisiting ordinary additive model evolution, but it does not eliminate concern for silent semantic reinterpretation of populated governance fields or low-cost conformance aliases.

overall.oneLineConclusion: NamingSystem keeps its R4 identity and core instance shape; R6 migration is targeted around optional canonical metadata, jurisdiction/date semantics, identifier-type tooling, one operation behavior, and search metadata aliases.

reasoning.thesisMd: NamingSystem is not a resource where a broad R4-to-R6 instance migration program is already unavoidable. The same-name resource remains, required core elements remain, and the report found no hard or potential old-valid/new-invalid instance breaks. The important work is per-change: preserve or document compatibility for semantic governance fields and conformance/API metadata while treating additive R6-only metadata and expanded codes as ordinary targeted migration tasks.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The largest structural change is CanonicalResource-style metadata added as optional elements (`url`, `version`, lifecycle/review fields, contacts, related artifacts, and `uniqueId.authoritative`). Existing R4 instances generally remain structurally valid in R6. The non-mechanical parts are narrower: `jurisdiction` changes meaning from intended-use region toward maintainer-authority jurisdiction, `date` is aligned with last significant change and new lifecycle fields, `uniqueId.type` adds two required-binding codes for R6 instances, and behavior metadata changes affect `$preferred-id` and canonical SearchParameter identities.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because there is no broad resource redesign or identity replacement, preventing each avoidable local break still has high leverage. Low FMM means not every break warrants standards rework, but it is still worthwhile to preserve low-cost aliases and avoid silent semantic changes where populated R4 data can be misread.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking opportunity is `NamingSystem.jurisdiction`: R6 could have preserved the R4 intended-use meaning on the existing path and added a separate maintainer-jurisdiction representation or clearer transition rule. The canonical SearchParameter consolidation also appears amenable to deprecated alias resources or equivalent canonical URL handling. By contrast, optional metadata additions, the weakened `NamingSystem.type` binding, and the widened `uniqueId.type` code system are mostly proportional evolution rather than avoidable R4-to-R6 breaks.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior surface matters but does not create a resource-level migration program. `$preferred-id` changes multiple-match behavior from mandatory error toward preference/date-based resolution, which can break tests or clients that relied on ambiguity errors but is proportionate to the operation's purpose. SearchParameter canonical URL consolidation is more standards-review-worthy because conformance tooling often keys on canonical SearchParameter URLs even when query parameters remain usable. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as background.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = No` with `preserve-compatibility-per-change`; this review agrees with that resource-level posture. The agreement is based on the actual migration shape rather than counts: no hard R4-to-R6 instance break, stable resource identity, and only targeted semantic/API issues. The aggregate should not be used to discount the specific jurisdiction and SearchParameter alias concerns.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the resource-level shape because the local R4/R6 StructureDefinitions and behavior reports are available. Remaining uncertainty is mainly implementation prevalence and final R6 ballot volatility, plus external terminology expansion details for some bindings.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional canonical and governance metadata fields that R4 cannot natively carry
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the broadest structural change, but it is optional and primarily creates R6-to-R4 fidelity risk. It supports the conclusion that NamingSystem is extended toward canonical/governance metadata rather than remodeled in a way that forces old R4 instances through a major transform.

findingConsiderations.title: NamingSystem.jurisdiction now describes maintainer authority jurisdiction and is deprecated in favor of useContext jurisdiction
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This same-path semantic change can silently reinterpret populated R4 data. Even with FMM 1, jurisdiction can drive registry filtering and governance decisions, and a modest less-breaking base design appears plausible.

findingConsiderations.title: Lifecycle metadata semantics shifted around date, purpose, publisher, and review/effective dates
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `date` remains required `dateTime`, so this is not a hard break, but publication/audit workflows may need version-aware interpretation as R6 separates approval, review, effective period, and purpose metadata.

findingConsiderations.title: NamingSystem.uniqueId.type required binding adds iri-stem and v2csmnemonic codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The path is central and closed-enum tooling must update, but R6 retained all R4 codes and only widened the required value set. This is a local codegen/validator and R6-to-R4 downgrade issue, not evidence of unavoidable R4 instance migration.

findingConsiderations.title: NamingSystem.type binding changed from extensible IdentifierType to preferred NamingSystemIdentifierSystemType
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element shape is unchanged and R6 weakens the binding from extensible to preferred. It may change terminology advice or picklists, but it does not materially affect the resource-level compatibility posture.

findingConsiderations.title: Multiple matching identifiers change from mandatory error to preference/date-based resolution
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a direct NamingSystem runtime behavior change. It can break clients or tests expecting ambiguity errors, but the new preference/date resolution is aligned with the operation's purpose and does not force a resource-wide data migration.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: NamingSystem is directly affected. Runtime query names may survive, but canonical SearchParameter identity is important conformance metadata for servers, CapabilityStatements, and generators; deprecated aliases or equivalence guidance look low-cost relative to the tooling break.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This was considered as shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context, but it is not NamingSystem-specific and therefore does not drive the NamingSystem resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared search metadata issue may affect generic clients, but under the assigned scope it remains background context rather than a NamingSystem-specific migration driver.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit `NamingSystem.jurisdiction` semantics and publish explicit migration guidance or a less-breaking design that avoids silently treating intended-use jurisdiction as maintainer-authority jurisdiction.
Provide deprecated aliases or formal equivalence guidance for NamingSystem-related canonical SearchParameter URLs that were consolidated into CanonicalResource/MetadataResource definitions.
Update NamingSystem validators, generated enums, and conversion guidance for `uniqueId.type` additions and the R6 `$preferred-id` multiple-match behavior.
Document R6-to-R4 preservation strategy for optional canonical/governance metadata and the newer lifecycle fields so downgrades do not silently drop registry governance information.

caveats: R6 input is ballot4, so final R6 content may differ.
No live terminology expansion service or production prevalence data was used beyond the supplied local reports and packages.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, not scored as NamingSystem-specific findings.
